read off the Oscillator tab, where the seven shapes are drawn as waveform icons with abbreviated text. Every position's wording differs from the catalog (SIN vs Sine, PUL vs Pulse); positions 5 and 6 differ in MEANING, not just spelling - see the note there. OSC 1 must be switched on before the shapes appear. The parameter is marked hidden='true' in the catalog and is on the screen anyway, which is why 'absent' is never derived from that flag.

THE CATALOG HAS PINK AND WHITE SWAPPED. Driven and read back on 2026-09-14: wire position 5, which the catalog calls 'Pink NS', shows WHT, and position 6, which it calls 'White NS', shows PNK. Both were set at once on the two oscillators of one Mono Synth and read together, so neither reading can be a stale screen. This is the same shape of error as the metronome names - a caller asking for pink noise by the catalog's name gets white.
